earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog doee1238 lists only classification/endangerment works (Gonzales 2002; Dimmendaal & Voeltz 2007); no grammar or phonology of Doe located online.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record doee1238 (bibliography: Gonzales 2002; Johnston 1919-22; Stuhlmann 1894, 1916-17; Baur & Le Roy 1882-1893; Dimmendaal & Voeltz 2007; Bastin et al. 1999; Nurse 1988; Grollemund et al. 2015)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; no grammar, sketch or phonology is registered for Doe.

sources.citation: Legère, Karsten. 2014. Documenting the Dowe language. London: SOAS, Endangered Languages Archive, deposit dk0269 (ELDP SG0213; hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0000-A91D-4). https://www.elararchive.org/dk0269
sources.note: Deposit landing page read: audio/video of Dowe oral traditions (Msata and Miono wards, Bagamoyo District, 2012-2013) with transcriptions in a Swahili-based orthography and Swahili translations, ethnobotanical photos, a map. No grammar sketch, phonology or orthography statement is listed; page says nothing about stress or tone.

sources.citation: Legère, Karsten (ed.). 2013. Bantu languages and linguistics: papers in memory of Dr. Rugatiri D. K. Mekacha (Bayreuth African Studies 91). Bayreuth. [Table of contents from DNB, d-nb.info/1045715263/04]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: TOC checked only, to test whether Legère (who did Dowe fieldwork 2012-13) published a Dowe chapter here: he did not (his chapter is on language in the Tanganyika liberation struggle). Nothing on Doe.

sources.citation: Petzell, Malin & Harald Hammarström. 2013. Grammatical and lexical comparison of the Greater Ruvu Bantu languages. Nordic Journal of African Studies 22(3): 129-157. doi:10.53228/njas.v22i3.159
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sample is Kagulu G12, Zigua G31, Kwere G32, Zalamo G33, Nguu G34, Luguru G35, Kami G36, Kutu G37; Doe (G301) is not included (0 mentions in the text layer) and no stress statement appears for any language.

sources.note: All negative: no grammar, sketch, thesis or phonology article on Doe/Dowe was found in any of these indexes; Legère's catalogued post-2012 output covers Akie, Vidunda, Kwangali, linguistic landscapes, ethnobotany, not Dowe.
